result.title: PhyMo: Learning Physical Dynamics with Accurate and Continuous Motion from Multi-View Videos
result.summary: Recovering dynamic 3D scene geometry, appearance, and the physical motion states that govern scene evolution from multi-view videos is important yet challenging. A key difficulty is that appearance can be deceptive. Under rendering supervision alone, a model may fit the observed images by changing color or opacity to compensate for inaccurate deformation, rather than recovering the true evolving geometry and motion. This issue is especially severe in scenes with fast or locally complex motion, where inaccurate trajectories can still produce plausible images over the observed frames, but lead to unreliable reconstruction and discontinuous future prediction. In this paper, we propose PhyMo, a framework for learning evolving dynamics from multi-view videos. We introduce a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation that drives the model to recover accurate motion from deformation, rather than relying on appearance shortcuts to explain observed motion. On top of this, we propose a Continuous Motion Evolution module with bidirectional kinematic continuity constraint to promote temporally consistent evolution of displacement, velocity, and acceleration. Together, these designs yield geometrically faithful interpolation and continuous motion extrapolation. Experiments on four dynamic scene benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.

AI.brief_summary: PhyMo 从多视角视频中重建动态 3D 场景的几何、外观与物理运动状态，提出运动感知轨迹表示以阻止模型用颜色、透明度等外观变化掩盖错误形变，并加入双向运动学连续性约束，使位移、速度与加速度在时间上连续演化，从而支持几何忠实的插值与运动外推。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「appearance shortcut」的诊断与用显式轨迹表示强制内部状态承载真实运动，可能与 VLM 中视觉旁路、信息坍缩的检验形成概念类比；连续性约束也可供核查 latent 状态演化监督的设计，但跨领域迁移性尚待评估。
